Claim: Capitol Police Officer Brian Sicknick was killed after being struck in the head with a fire extinguisher by Trump supporters during the Jan. 6 Capitol riot.
Ended: Feb 12, 2021 (NYT update questioning cause); Apr 19, 2021 (D.C. medical examiner: natural causes/stroke)
Who_Pushed_It: The New York Times (initial report citing two law-enforcement officials); widespread cable/network amplification; House impeachment memorandum citing the extinguisher claim
Approximate_Duration: about 5 weeks until NYT update; about 3.5 months until medical examiner ruling
Notes: Sources were anonymous LE officials; ME ruled natural causes (stroke). Assault of officers including chemical spray still documented separately.

Claim: UN Ambassador Nikki Haley was responsible for a $52,701 curtain purchase at the UN envoy residence.
Ended: Sep 14, 2018 (NYT editors' note: unfair impression; lease/curtains decided under Obama admin)
Who_Pushed_It: The New York Times
Approximate_Duration: 1 day until editors' note and headline/photo change
Notes: Editors' note: article should not have focused on Haley nor used her photo.

Claim: ICE used Facebook data to find and track immigrants for immigration violations (as framed in original Intercept headline/lede).
Ended: Mar 26–27, 2018 (Intercept correction: documents showed a criminal suspect, not an immigration target; editor Ryan Grim inserted the error)
Who_Pushed_It: The Intercept (editor Ryan Grim); viral amplification framing Trump ICE as hunting immigrants via Facebook
Notes: Reporter Lee Fang's filing was accurate; Grim changed 'suspect' to 'immigrant.'

Claim: In a 1998 People magazine interview, Trump said he would run as a Republican because they are 'the dumbest group of voters in the country.'
Began: Oct 2015 (viral origin); widely recirculated through first term including 2020
Ended: No ending date (still repeated); FactCheck.org and Snopes rated False; People found no such interview
Who_Pushed_It: Viral social media memes; repeated Facebook/Twitter recirculation during first term
Notes: People confirmed no 1998 interview/quote. Claim originated pre-inauguration but was actively pushed during first term (e.g., Snopes May 2020 update).

Claim: The WHO offered COVID-19 test kits to the United States and the Trump administration refused/rejected them.
Ended: Mar 16, 2020 (PolitiFact Mostly False; WHO said no discussions about providing kits to the U.S.)
Who_Pushed_It: Joe Biden (Democratic debate); viral Facebook posts
Approximate_Duration: days of campaign amplification; fact-check next day
Notes: U.S. developed its own CDC test; WHO typically does not supply kits to countries with advanced lab capacity.

Claim: The Trump administration made no effort to get U.S. medical experts into China early in the COVID outbreak.
Ended: Apr 1, 2020 (FactCheck.org: False; CDC offered a team Jan 6, 2020)
Who_Pushed_It: Joe Biden (CNN virtual town hall)
Notes: China limited access; U.S. offers were documented by HHS/Azar.

Claim: Trump 'cut' or 'slashed' CDC funding (presented as enacted cuts, not merely proposed).
Ended: Mar 3, 2020 (FactCheck.org: Congress rejected proposed cuts and often increased CDC funding)
Who_Pushed_It: Joe Biden; Mike Bloomberg; other Democrats
Approximate_Duration: weeks of campaign messaging; ongoing variants
Notes: Trump proposed CDC cuts; Congress did not enact them. Accurate to say he 'tried' to cut.

Claim: Trump 'hasn't allowed his scientists to speak' / was 'muzzling' CDC/NIH scientists on COVID-19.
Ended: Mar 1–3, 2020 (FactCheck.org: went too far; Fauci said he was not muzzled; clearance process after Pence took over)
Who_Pushed_It: Joe Biden (CNN, ABC This Week)
Notes: Scientists were told to clear appearances through the task force; they continued public interviews.

Claim: Donald Trump says he will 'terminate' Social Security if re-elected.
Ended: Aug 12, 2020 (PolitiFact Mostly False: he discussed terminating the payroll tax funding source, not ending Social Security benefits)
Who_Pushed_It: Social Security Works (Facebook post/advocacy)
Approximate_Duration: days of viral Facebook spread; variants recurred in later campaigns
Notes: Distinct from later 2024 Harris/Biden 'intends to cut Social Security' items already in the 85.

Claim: Trump said, 'People are dying who have never died before,' during COVID briefings.
Ended: Mar 19, 2020 (PolitiFact Pants on Fire: no evidence in transcripts/databases)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral Facebook posts
Notes: Fabricated quote attributed to Trump.

Claim: In The Art of the Deal, Trump wrote that 'being an atheist gives me an edge in every deal' and that 'Christians are too moral for business.'
Ended: Apr 17, 2019 (PolitiFact Pants on Fire: fabricated quote not in the book)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral Facebook meme posts

Claim: Trump 'lied' about not knowing the pandemic office was disbanded, because he earlier defended cutting that team when he said 'some of the people we cut.'
Ended: Mar 20, 2020 (FactCheck.org: Feb 26 remarks answered a question about proposed CDC/NIH/WHO budget cuts, not the NSC pandemic office)
Who_Pushed_It: Democratic National Committee; Protect Our Care; Independent (UK) framing; celebrity/journalist retweets
Approximate_Duration: about 1 week of viral clip framing
Notes: NSC global health office was reorganized in 2018; separate from the Feb 26 budget-cut Q&A.

Claim: Trump fired the 'entire' pandemic response team in 2018.
Began: Mar 2020 (viral posts; Bloomberg/Biden variants earlier Feb–Mar 2020)
Ended: Mar 25–26, 2020 (Reuters: partly false; some staff reassigned under reorganized NSC structure)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral social media posts/images; Mike Bloomberg ('fired the pandemic team'); Joe Biden ('eliminated' the directorate)
Approximate_Duration: weeks of viral/campaign claims in early COVID period
Notes: Directorate was disbanded/reorganized May 2018 under Bolton; 'entire team fired' overstates.

Claim: The New York Times captioned a photo of Angela Bassett as Trump adviser Omarosa Manigault Newman.
Ended: Sep 18–19, 2018 (NYT acknowledgment/correction for early print editions)
Who_Pushed_It: The New York Times (wire photo caption error)
Notes: Wrong photo of a Trump administration figure; Poynter listed among 2018 serious corrections.

Claim: Trump said eliminating the White House pandemic office was among the 'very first' things his administration did.
Ended: Apr 1, 2020 (FactCheck.org: happened in May 2018, well into year two—not among first actions)
Who_Pushed_It: Joe Biden (CNN town hall characterization of timing)
Notes: Office elimination itself is documented; the 'first things' timing claim was wrong.

Claim: Celebrities' viral post: Trump 'cut funding to the CDC,' 'fired the Pandemic Response Team,' 'refused WHO tests,' and 'wasted two weeks calling this outbreak a Democrat hoax' (as a package of established facts).
Ended: Mar 17, 2020 (PolitiFact Mostly False on the package)
Who_Pushed_It: Translate Trump tweet; D.L. Hughley and other celebrities via Instagram
Notes: COVID-'hoax' fragment overlaps item 56 in the 85; included for the multi-claim package rating. Skip if merging with #56.

Claim: House Judiciary Committee Republicans voted to 'allow Trump to DEPORT U.S. citizens to a foreign country.'
Ended: May 6, 2025 (PolitiFact Mostly False: voting down a Democratic amendment did not confer legal authority to deport citizens)
Who_Pushed_It: Rep. Eric Swalwell; Rep. Daniel Goldman; Rep. Pramila Jayapal
Approximate_Duration: about 1 week of social/political amplification until fact-check
Notes: U.S. case law still bars deporting citizens; committee vote left status quo.

Claim: DOGE/Trump SSA staffing and procedure changes are cutting or eliminating Social Security benefits / setting up privatization that will 'rip away benefits.'
Ended: Apr 9, 2025 (FactCheck.org: no proposed change to legally mandated benefit amounts; privatization claims speculative)
Who_Pushed_It: Democratic National Committee; Sen. Bernie Sanders; Sen. Chuck Schumer; Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Ron Wyden; Rep. John Larson (MSNBC)
Approximate_Duration: weeks of March–April 2025 messaging; variants ongoing
Notes: Administrative disruption concerns may be real; conflating that with statutory benefit cuts was misleading. Distinct from 2024 campaign 'intends to cut SS' items 44–46.

Claim: Project 2025 / Trump allies' plan calls for restricting access to IVF and contraception (as a blanket plan Trump would enact).
Ended: Jul 24, 2024 (PolitiFact Mostly False: no specific IVF ban; no general ban of standard contraception)
Who_Pushed_It: Kamala Harris; Democratic campaign messaging
Notes: Document does recommend limits on some emergency contraception coverage and Planned Parenthood funding; not a general IVF/contraception ban. Distinct from pregnancy-registry items 42–43, 55.

Claim: As a result of the 'Big Beautiful Bill,' 15 million Americans have already been thrown off the healthcare they need.
Ended: Apr 30, 2026 (PolitiFact Mostly False: premature; ~1 million ACA enrollment drop so far; CBO projected ~10M uninsured by 2034 from the law)
Who_Pushed_It: Sen. Bernie Sanders
Approximate_Duration: days–weeks of repeated claims; fact-check about 1 week later
Notes: Future coverage losses projected; 'have been thrown off' past-tense overstated.

Claim: ICE secretly deported Allentown, PA 'grandfather' Luis Leon to Guatemala (and related claims he died in custody).
Ended: Jul 21–25, 2025 (Morning Call unpublished stories; Guatemala no match; photos were of a different man who died in 2021; DHS/ICE said never arrested/deported)
Who_Pushed_It: The Morning Call (Allentown); viral social amplification
Approximate_Duration: about 5–7 days until unpublishing and photo debunk
Notes: Verify via outlet's own update and AP/Guatemala denials; do not rely solely on DHS press release rhetoric.

Claim: ICE deportation flights are throwing migrants into the middle of the ocean (and related chained bodies/Sudan missing-plane claims).
Ended: Jul 15, 2025 (PolitiFact Pants on Fire; flight tracker said no basis after 40,000+ flights)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral TikTok/X posts
Approximate_Duration: about 2 weeks of viral spread until Pants on Fire rating
Notes: Spain shore bodies unrelated (North Africa migrant smuggling, per reporting).

Claim: Trump ordered the cutting down of iconic weeping willow trees outside the Kennedy Center.
Ended: Sep 2, 2026 (Snopes False; facilities VP sworn testimony: trees removed for safety/decay; Trump not involved in decision)
Who_Pushed_It: Adam Parkhomenko (former Clinton adviser); viral social posts
Notes: Trees removed ~Oct 2025 for maintenance per center testimony.

Claim: ICE arrested/deported Mexican rescue volunteers who helped during Texas floods, with Gov. Greg Abbott saying he supported it.
Ended: Jul 14, 2025 (Snopes: no evidence of such arrests; Abbott clip was AI deepfake)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral TikTok/Instagram/X posts with AI-altered Abbott video
Notes: Mexican volunteers did assist; no credible reports of ICE arresting them.

Claim: Trump’s tariffs cost each Michigan household $5,619.
Ended: Sep 17, 2026 (PolitiFact Mostly False: figure divides importer-paid tariffs by households; costs not borne solely by MI households)
Who_Pushed_It: Abdul El-Sayed (Democratic U.S. Senate nominee, Michigan)
Approximate_Duration: about 2 weeks until PolitiFact Mostly False

Claim: It is 'official' that Trump signed an order giving taxpayers a $5,000 'DOGE dividend' stimulus check.
Ended: Feb 26, 2025 (PolitiFact False: idea floated; no signed order or official program)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral Facebook/X posts with edited Treasury-check graphics
Notes: Trump said he liked the concept; not enacted.

Claim: ICE agents raided Los Angeles' Gratts Learning Academy during a June 2025 graduation, forcing parents without papers to flee and leave children.
Ended: Jun 6–10, 2025 (LAUSD superintendent and district: false; no such raid)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral Instagram/TikTok video of a school worker; multi-platform shares
Approximate_Duration: days until district denial; PolitiFact False Jun 13
Notes: Distinct from Chicago Hamline Elementary item 19 in the 85.

Claim: Trump ordered U.S. borders closed starting July 1 with no set reopening date.
Ended: Jul 2, 2025 (PolitiFact False: no such EO in White House/Federal Register)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral TikTok posts
Notes: PolitiFact found no evidence of such an indefinite border-closure executive order.

Claim: DOGE discovered $2.7 trillion in improper federal payments (as a DOGE discovery).
Ended: Feb 18, 2025 (PolitiFact: DOGE subcommittee didn't 'discover' that figure; it came from prior GAO estimates)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral social media posts; Real America's Voice reporter Brian Glenn (premise in question); Karoline Leavitt (appeared to accept premise); Elon Musk (reposted)
Notes: About Trump/DOGE claims of discovery; figure predated DOGE.

Claim: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced Americans can get a $4,800 subsidy because DOGE cuts found 'extra money.'
Ended: Feb 21, 2025 (PolitiFact False: altered video splicing fake script onto real Leavitt clip; no such subsidy)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral Facebook page 'American Help' / scam-style posts
Notes: Altered video attributed false DOGE subsidy announcement to Trump admin official.

Claim: Elon Musk / DOGE contracted a helicopter and began dispersing DOGE payments by raining cash on California.
Ended: Feb 24, 2025 (PolitiFact Pants on Fire: spliced 2021 Carlsbad armored-truck cash and 2023 Czech TV stunt)
Who_Pushed_It: Viral Facebook posts
Approximate_Duration: 1–2 days until Pants on Fire rating
Notes: False claim about Trump/DOGE dispersing savings; older unrelated clips.
